heading: Together, let's build an Orange County for everyone.
text: For over a decade, Orange County families have trusted Tiffany Moore Russell for her steady leadership and unwavering integrity. A proud Orange County native, Tiffany made history as the youngest person ever elected to the Orange County Commission—and later, as the first African American woman elected Clerk of Courts in both Orange County and the state of Florida.

heading: Together, let's build an Orange County for everyone.
text: In every role, from attorney to commissioner to clerk, she has led with principle, putting the community first. As Clerk, Tiffany prioritized fiscal accountability—returning unused emergency funds, investing in technology to safeguard public records, and streamlining court operations. She has worked tirelessly to ensure access to justice, including launching a self-help center for residents navigating the legal system without an attorney. Her leadership reflects a deep commitment to innovation, transparency, and doing what’s right for the people she serves.

heading: As a lifelong Orange County resident and dedicated public servant, I am running for Mayor because every resident deserves a stronger and more vibrant community.
text: As your next Orange County mayor, I will fight for quality services, more economic opportunities, and a responsive government that will put you first. Our community needs bold new leadership that listens, takes action, and delivers real results for families, businesses, and future generations. I have done the work to show you I am that leader. In this campaign, I will work to earn your vote and together we will build a new bold, thriving Orange County and I will earn your vote.

heading: As a lifelong Orange County resident and dedicated public servant, I am running for Mayor because every resident deserves a stronger and more vibrant community.
text: Elected to the Orange County Commission in 2006 to represent District 6, Tiffany became the youngest commissioner in county history. She served two terms before making history again in 2014 as the first African American female Clerk elected in Florida and the first African American Clerk in Orange County.

heading: As a lifelong Orange County resident and dedicated public servant, I am running for Mayor because every resident deserves a stronger and more vibrant community.
text: Statewide, Moore Russell serves on the FCCC Board of Directors and Executive Committee as President and is Vice Chair of the CCOC Executive Council, contributing to policy and governance at the state level.

heading: As a lifelong Orange County resident and dedicated public servant, I am running for Mayor because every resident deserves a stronger and more vibrant community.
text: Beyond her public service, she is an active member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc., Psi Theta Omega Chapter, and St. Mark AME Church in Orlando. She is married to Anthony K. Russell, Jr., and they have two sons, Anthony K. Russell III and Aiden K. Russell.

heading: As a lifelong Orange County resident and dedicated public servant, I am running for Mayor because every resident deserves a stronger and more vibrant community.
text: As a trained attorney, Moore Russell has been a champion for accessible justice, particularly for economically disadvantaged residents. She established the Lydia Gardner Self Help Center, the first of its kind in Orange County, providing low-cost legal assistance in family law, residential evictions, and small claims.
